Attached are Acme's redlines to the MSA and the proposed DPA Annex A. I've attached the redlines and a short change-log. Let me know if you want to discuss on a call.

On Thu, Sep 9, 2026 at 11:03 AM sergio.alvarez@redwood.com wrote:
> Hi Acme team — thanks for the redlines and the clear timeline. Sharing this with Law (Laura) and Security (Monica) to validate the flow-down asks.

Thanks — I've reviewed the attached MSA redlines. High-level legal perspective:

1) Prior written consent: we should avoid an absolute prior-consent veto for any new subprocessor; propose a middle-ground: "Customer's consent shall not be unreasonably withheld; for subprocessors that will have access to Customer Data, Redwood will provide notice and a right to object within 15 days. If no objection is received, consent is deemed granted."

2) Flow-down scope: limit to "processing activities relating to the performance of the Agreement" rather than a broad blanket flow-down.

3) Audit evidence: acceptable forms should be enumerated (SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, or, if not available, a third-party security attestation). Requiring raw audit artifacts is not acceptable; we can provide auditor reports and a signed attestation.

4) DPA annex: I'll attach a redline with suggested language for the subprocessor clause and an alternate Consent/Notice flow.

I'll also ask Privacy to prepare an attestation template we can provide to Acme for subprocessors.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redline_dpa_annex_laura_20260909.docx (docx)

From: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
To: contracts@acme-corp.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme MSA redlines and subcontractor flow-down — Redwood counter and subproc list

Acme Contracts — appreciate the quick turnaround. Please find below our proposed path and attachments. Key points:

1) Subprocessor intent list: attached (names and functional roles). We'll provide a formal, live list and commit to notice before onboarding any additional subprocessor with access to Acme data.

2) Consent/objection timeline: Redwood proposes notice + 15 calendar day objection window; consent deemed granted if no objection is raised. For critical subprocessors (e.g., those doing persistent storage or managed logging) we're open to a short call to discuss.

3) Audit evidence: Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II reports for primary infrastructure processors and will provide attestation templates for smaller subprocessors. We suggest enumerating acceptable evidence in the DPA (SOC2, ISO27001, or auditor attestation).

4) DPA Annex: Laura has provided a redline (attached) with our preferred edits.

If this is acceptable, we can prepare a DocuSign packet (MSA + DPA) and target execution by 2026-09-22. If you prefer, let's schedule a 30-minute alignment call Monday 9/13.

Thanks,
Sergio
